name: Automation Triggers

# Streamlit has no built-in background job scheduler at all. Both of
# the checks below (weather emails, and overdue-task/expiring-permit
# escalations) have real logic already built in app.py that decides
# EVERY time whether anything is actually due to send — but neither
# one can run on its own; something has to actually call it. Before
# this workflow existed, neither ever did, on any kind of reliable
# schedule — weather emails never arrived at all, and escalations
# only fired "once per session, if a Superintendent happens to open
# the Task Dashboard," which could mean an overdue task at 2am gets
# zero alert to anyone until someone next happens to log in.
#
# This workflow is that missing timer, for both. It runs hourly and
# does nothing but two plain HTTP GETs to the app's own automation-
# trigger endpoints — each one's own cooldown/due-check logic decides
# whether anything actually needs sending this time, so running this
# hourly doesn't mean hourly emails, it just means neither check is
# ever more than an hour late.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch: {}   # lets you trigger a manual test run from the Actions tab

jobs:
  ping:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Ping the weather-check automation endpoint
        run: |
          curl -sf "https://mine-task-tracker-ljc2ppwmwiwtfqwykn2by5.streamlit.app/?weather_check=1&token=${{ secrets.AUTOMATION_TRIGGER_TOKEN }}" \
            -o weather_response.json
          cat weather_response.json
        # -f makes curl itself fail (non-zero exit) on an HTTP error
        # status, so a broken URL/token shows up as a failed red run
        # in the Actions tab rather than silently doing nothing.

      - name: Ping the escalations automation endpoint
        run: |
          curl -sf "https://mine-task-tracker-ljc2ppwmwiwtfqwykn2by5.streamlit.app/?run_escalations=1&token=${{ secrets.AUTOMATION_TRIGGER_TOKEN }}" \
            -o escalations_response.json
          cat escalations_response.json
